tasks.instructions:
Experiment E1 (single focused session, operator brief 2026-10-11, r11): only the sizes B >= 373 (tc_h nb1 and nb2). Keep the B <= 256 paths byte-identical to r10. Read ledger H28-H30 and tricks.md sections 2 and 5 first.

Why this round: a clean-room paper session saw only the problem and the hardware, never our kernel. It independently ranked our layout first: W rows in M = 256 per pair, the batch in N up to 512, LDG converters, kind::f16. It estimated 95 us at 919 and 53 at 512 on the portal, with only about 4 us of overhead per call. Our main loop already runs at that efficiency (nb2 about 1346 clk per k-block against 1299 ideal at N = 464). The gap is the time outside the loop. r10 timelines (rented, flush, globaltimer):
- 919: first full about 9 us, item 0 last full 43.5, epilogue to 48.9, tfree 49.9, item 1 first full 51.7 (8.2 us MMA idle), last full 85.5, end 92.4.
- 384: prologue end 2.8, emb slice converted 5.9-6.4, grid emb counter seen 7.4, first full 9.2, last full 45.6, epilogue end 50.2, kernel end 51-53, harness 56.5.
On the portal (about 1.5 GHz) the MMA loop stretches by 1.3-1.4x, but these overheads are latency and stay about the same. At 919 about 25 of the 112.5 us is outside the loop.

Portal targets: 691/773/853/919 at about 87/93/97/98 us (now 101.6/107.1/111.7/112.5) and 373-512 about 6 us faster (now 59.8/59.7/64.6/68.4). Predicted mean about 0.71-0.72 (now 0.694).

Levers, biggest first:
1. nb2 drain overlap (the paper session's idea). Split each item's accumulator into acc0 and acc1 (e.g. 256 + 208 columns at 919). Issue the last s k-blocks (s <= stages) of acc0 before those of acc1 and commit acc0 to its own barrier. The epilogue then drains acc0 while acc1 finishes. Item 1's acc0 MMAs start as soon as acc0's columns are drained, while acc1 drains, and the W producer and converters keep running into item 1 across the boundary instead of waiting for the epilogue. Work out how many of item 1's k-blocks can run on acc0 alone before stages must wait for acc1 (4 stages at 919). Consider an uneven split, or the drain order, if that helps. r10 concluded that this needs spare TMEM; check that claim, since item 1's acc0 reuses acc0's columns. Measure the idle gap and the end-of-kernel drain with the same timeline.
2. Start the MMA sooner, mainly at nb2 where it adds directly to the time. Possible routes:
   - a relaxed cluster barrier in the prologue (r10: 2.8 -> 1.0-1.3 us);
   - per-k-block emb readiness (convert emb in k order and publish one counter per k-block range, so the first stages do not wait for the whole emb);
   - each pair converting its own first emb k-blocks from fp32 while the grid-wide conversion finishes.
   Target: first full <= 4-5 us at 919. r10 showed that nb1 does not gain from this (it is DRAM-bound from its first load), so measure each regime separately.
3. nb1 (373-512) is DRAM-bound. The in-kernel W stream takes about 43 us against 38.8 for the same pattern alone, and then a 4-5 us epilogue (28 MB of writes) runs serially.
   (a) Use the same acc0-first ordering so the acc0 writes overlap the stream tail. The total bytes are fixed, so the overlap is free DRAM time.
   (b) Close the stream gap. Look at converter convoying at the group bar.sync and per-pair DRAM-rate imbalance (last full spread 44.0-47.9 us), for example a dynamic split of the last k-range or tiles. Do not retry L2 prefetch ahead of the ring (r9: +5-10 us) unless a probe shows the converters are latency-bound.
4. Optional, only if levers 1-2 land with time to spare: run both items of a W tile on two pairs in the same wave (wave 1 = tiles 0-35 x 2 items, wave 2 = tiles 36-71), so W comes from DRAM once instead of twice (about 450 -> 226 MB at 919). It lowers DRAM traffic and power, but the portal loop is MMA-bound, so expect a small effect.
Do not build W-in-TMEM (A from tensor memory), cluster-4 DSMEM sharing or an L2 fp16 ring this round: the paper estimates show no gain while the main loop is not shared-memory-bound.

Method:
- Probe each lever in isolation, with the r10-e1 kernel as the control in the same container: 3 interleaved rounds, harness_time.
- Report the globaltimer timeline (first full, last full per item, MMA idle, epilogue end) at 384 and 919, before and after.
- Predict portal times with the main loop x1.33-1.42 at nb2 and x1.09-1.21 at nb1, and overheads x1.0-1.1.
- Before shipping, run run_tests 16/16 x 10 rounds and record max |err| per B (it must stay < 1.8e-3).
tasks.success: 16/16 x 10 rounds, max |err| < 1.8e-3; in the same container as r10-e1: 691-919 >= 8% faster or 373-512 >= 6% faster; the 919 timeline shows MMA idle between items <= 3 us and/or first full <= 5 us; predicted portal score >= 0.705.
tasks.refuted_if: acc0-first ordering still leaves >= 6 us of MMA idle between items (ring dependency on acc1); per-k-block emb readiness does not bring first full below 7 us; nb1 epilogue overlap saves < 2 us. Record each with its numbers.
